positions.title: Web Manager
positions.locationName: W. P. Carey School of Business
positions.description:
◘ Manage all marketing web assets and contribute to the design and implementation of university standards, web update request support and working with unit needs.
◘ Work with cross-functional teams to execute critical projects, and improve site experience and performance.
◘ Onboard, train, supervise and mentor direct reports to assist with the completion of web updates.
◘ Lead employee training as new technologies get implemented.
◘ Manage projects, including scoping project requirements, identifying timelines and taking a leading role in coordinating cross-team digital projects.

positions.title: Marketing Web Developer
positions.locationName: W. P. Carey School of Business
positions.description:
◘ Overseeing the process of web request updates across school web properties. Including the onboarding, training, supervising and mentoring student workers to assist with the completion of web updates.
◘ Project management, including scoping project requirements, identifying timelines and taking a leading role in coordinating cross-team digital projects.
◘ Designed wireframes, high-res comps for all web projects for desktop and mobile.
◘ Front-end development utilizing HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript leveraging the Bootstrap and Foundation framework.
◘ Worked closely and collaboratively with backend Web developer in IT, to scope and communicate technical requirements that support business objectives.

positions.title: Web Specialist (IT)
positions.locationName: W. P. Carey School of Business
positions.description:
◘ Research, design and develop web projects that incorporate the use of prebuilt tools as well as self-built solutions using standards-compliant jQuery, HTML and CSS.
◘ Help set up and monitor web analytics to identify areas of improvement.
◘ Optimize existing sites, by cleaning up and adapting modern technologies to improve site performance and UX.
◘ Conduct research through focus groups, to guide UX/UI decision-making.
◘ Implement multivariate testing that help evaluate different designs choices in respect to their impact on conversion rates.
◘ Analyze rival websites to dissect and identify strengths and weaknesses of their approach to advise the development of new web-based projects. 
◘ Design and develop cross-platform email templates.
◘ Train technical and non-technical staff on various web topics - HTML, CSS and email marketing platform Silverpop.
◘ Work closely with the Marketing team to build the new W. P. Carey site. A responsive, HTML5 site built on Drupal. Help create the design of the site and aid through the entire production of the site by working collaboratively with the backend developer.
◘ Act as the liaison for the Marketing department, interfacing with the IT team to help implement, troubleshoot and install new technologies.

positions.title: Graphic/Web Designer
positions.description: Web design, video and photography for a grant funded project. Designed, coded and themed a Student Resource Portal on Telligent (a proprietary content management system). Created an online virtual tour using HTML, CSS, jQuery and the Google maps API; was responsible for the concept, design and coding of the entire project. It also involved shooting video and conducting interviews.

positions.title: Graphic Designer
positions.description: Graphic Design Student for the New Media Innovation Lab

projects.title: Camp Carey Microsite
projects.description: Microsite to differentiate the W. P. Carey School of Business undergraduate experience, to showcase the benefits of attending Camp Carey and to drive increased registrations.

projects.title: Mobile Responsive Email Program
projects.description: Implemented mobile responsive email templates across all graduate marketing and recruiting emails. More than 250 email templates were rolled out, many with dynamic content elements. The project required team collaboration across design, content and development. Goals of the project included increasing open and click-through-rates (CTR), reducing lead engagement timeline and increasing conversion. To date, open rates across the automated nurture programs have gone from around 2% CTR to approximately 14%.
